items.title: Section: The Four Bases of Power Open — Aspiration-Concentration in Detail

items.zh: 從此復修四三摩地。謂欲三摩地、勤三摩地、心三摩地、觀三摩地。當知由欲增上力所得三摩地，名欲三摩地；由勤增上力所得三摩地，名勤三摩地；由心增上力所得三摩地，名心三摩地；由觀增上力所得三摩地，名觀三摩地。若於是時純生樂欲，生樂欲已，於諸所有惡不善法自性、因緣、過患、對治，正審思察，起一境念。於諸善法自性、因緣、功德、出離，正審思察，住一境念。即由如是多修習故，觸一境性。於諸所有惡不善法現行諸纏，能令遠離，而未永害煩惱隨眠。
items.en: From this point, one further cultivates the four kinds of concentration: aspiration-concentration, effort-concentration, mind-concentration, and investigation-concentration. When, at this time, a pure aspiration arises, and having arisen, one carefully and thoroughly examines the intrinsic nature, causes and conditions, faults, and antidote of all evil, unwholesome states, abiding in mindfulness on a single object — and likewise carefully and thoroughly examines the intrinsic nature, causes and conditions, merit, and liberating power of wholesome states, abiding in mindfulness on a single object — then, through this repeated cultivation, one attains one-pointedness. This is able to keep at a distance the manifest entanglements of all evil, unwholesome states, though it has not yet permanently destroyed the latent seeds of affliction.

items.zh: 是名欲增上力所得三摩地。

若於過去、未來、現在所緣境界，能順所有惡不善法，能順所有下中上品煩惱纏中，其未生者為令不生，其已生者為令斷滅，自策、自勵、發勤精進，行彼所緣，於彼境界自性、因緣、過患、對治，正審思察，住一境念。即由如是多安住故，能正生起心一境性。於諸所有惡不善法現行諸纏，能令遠離，而未永害煩惱隨眠。是名勤增上力所得三摩地。若復策發諸下劣心，或復制持諸掉舉心，又時時間修增上捨。由是因緣，於諸所有惡不善法，若能隨順惡不善法，及諸善法，若能隨順所有善法自性、因緣、過患、功德、對治、出離，正審思察，住一境念。即由如是多安住故，能正生起心一境性，廣說乃至。是名心增上力所得三摩地。
items.en: Regarding objects belonging to the past, future, or present that tend towards evil, unwholesome states … self-spurring, self-rousing, and diligent effort, carefully and thoroughly examining that object's nature, causes, faults, and antidote, abiding in mindfulness on a single object — through this repeated abiding, one-pointedness rightly arises. This is called the concentration attained through the power of effort. Further lifting a sunken mind, restraining an agitated one, and cultivating excellent equanimity from time to time — this is called the concentration attained through the power of mind.

items.zh: 若於能順惡不善法，作意思惟為不如理；復於能順所有善法，作意思惟以為如理。如是遠離彼諸纏故，及能生起諸纏對治定為上首諸善法故，能令所有惡不善法皆不現行。

items.title: Section: Investigation-Concentration Closes All Four; Eight Kinds of Abandoning-Conditioning Open

items.zh: 便自思惟：我今為有現有惡不善法不覺知耶？為無現無惡不善法不覺知耶？我令應當遍審觀察。彼由觀察作意增上力故，自正觀察斷與未斷，正審思察，住一境念。即由如是多安住故，能正觸證心一境性。由是因緣，離增上慢，如實自知：我唯於纏心得解脫，未於一切一切隨眠心得解脫。我唯獲得及已修習諸纏對治定為上首所有善法，而未獲得及未修習隨眠對治。是名觀增上力所得三摩地。彼由如是四三摩地增上力故，已遠諸纏。復為永害一切一切惡不善法諸隨眠故，及為修集能對治彼諸善法故，便更生起樂欲、策勵，廣說如前修四正斷加行道理。彼於如是正修習時，有八斷行，為欲永害諸隨眠故，為三摩地得圓滿故，差別而轉。
items.en: One then reflects: "Is there, right now, some evil unwholesome state present that I am simply not aware of? Or is there, right now, none present, and I am not aware of that? I should thoroughly and carefully examine this." … Through this, one remains free of overestimation, truly knowing for oneself: "I have only gained freedom of mind from affliction's active manifestation — I have not yet gained freedom of mind from every latent seed of every kind." … This is called the concentration attained through the power of investigation. Having, through the power of these four concentrations, already kept the entanglements at a distance, and further wishing to permanently destroy every latent seed of evil, unwholesome states of every kind, and to cultivate the very wholesome states that counter them, one generates aspiration and self-spurring once again. In genuinely cultivating this way, there are eight kinds of conditioning, operating with their own distinct functions, for the sake of permanently destroying the latent seeds and for the sake of bringing concentration itself to full completion.

items.title: The Eight Kinds of Conditioning Named in Full

items.zh: 一者、欲。謂起如是希望樂欲：我於何時修三摩地當得圓滿？我於何時當能斷滅惡不善法所有隨眠？二者、策勵。謂乃至修所有對治，不捨加行。三者、信。謂不捨加行正安住故，於上所證，深生信解。四者、安。謂清淨信而為上首，心生歡喜；心歡喜故，漸次息除諸惡不善法品麁重。五者、念。謂九種相。於九種相安住其心，奢摩他品能攝持故。六者、正知。謂毘鉢舍那品慧。七者、思。謂心造作。於斷、未斷正觀察時，造作其心，發起能順止觀二品身業、語業。八者、捨。謂行過去、未來、現在隨順諸惡不善法中，心無染污、心平等性。
items.en: First, aspiration: generating this very wish — "When will my cultivation of concentration reach completion? When will I be able to destroy all the latent seeds of evil, unwholesome states?" Second, self-spurring: cultivating every antidote without abandoning the effort. Third, faith: through not abandoning the effort and remaining rightly settled in it, generating deep confidence in what is to be realised above. Fourth, pliancy: with pure faith leading the way, gladness arises in the mind; through that gladness, the grossness of evil, unwholesome states is gradually calmed and removed. Fifth, mindfulness: the nine aspects, the mind abiding in them, sustained by the calm-abiding factor. Sixth, clear comprehension: the wisdom belonging to insight. Seventh, volition: the mind's own activity — when carefully observing whether affliction is cut or not yet cut, activating the mind to generate bodily and verbal action in accord with calm-abiding and insight. Eighth, equanimity: whether engaging past, future, or present objects tending towards evil, unwholesome states, the mind remains undefiled, in a state of genuine evenness.

blocks.text: The four bases of power (神足), each a kind of concentration, and the eight "conditionings for abandoning" that accompany them. A short passage (0443b10) is untranslated.

Aspiration-concentration, effort-concentration, mind-concentration, investigation-concentration. In aspiration-concentration, "when a pure aspiration arises, one carefully examines the nature, causes, faults, and antidote of each unwholesome state". Venerable Miào Jìng: 纏 is affliction already active.

Effort-concentration: "self-spurring and diligent effort, carefully examining" objects that tend towards the unwholesome. Mind-concentration: "lifting a sunken mind, restraining an agitated one, cultivating equanimity from time to time".

"Is there, right now, some unwholesome state present that I am not aware of? Or none, and I am not aware of that?" "Through this, one remains free of overestimation, truly knowing: 'I have only gained freedom of mind from active affliction, not yet from its seeds.'" Venerable Miào Jìng: a question one should ask oneself honestly.

Aspiration ("When will my cultivation reach completion?"), effort, faith, pliancy ("with faith leading, gladness arises; through gladness, grossness ceases"), mindfulness, clear comprehension, volition ("the mind's own activity"; Venerable Miào Jìng: like a commander directing troops), and equanimity.

quiz.q: What are the four concentrations, and why are they named aspiration, effort, mind, and investigation?
options: these four are causes of concentration; named after the cause
quiz.why: "From this point, one further cultivates the four kinds of concentration: aspiration-concentration, effort-concentration, mind-concentration, and investigation-concentration." Venerable Miào Jìng: aspiration, effort, mind, and investigation are causes of concentration, which is the result; they are named after the cause.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe "a pure aspiration arises"?
options: dropping everything else and delighting only in sitting
quiz.why: "When, at this time, a pure aspiration arises, one carefully examines the nature, causes, faults, and antidote of evil states, abiding in mindfulness on a single object." Venerable Miào Jìng: everything else is set down and one simply delights in sitting — that is "pure aspiration."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "self-spurring, self-rousing, and diligent effort" in effort-concentration?
options: one "effort" expressed across times: past, future, present
quiz.why: "Self-spurring, self-rousing, and diligent effort, carefully examining that object's nature, causes, faults, and antidote." Master Cháng Bǎi: one word, "effort," expressed for different times — diligent regarding past, future, and present.

quiz.q: What methods does mind-concentration use, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain equanimity?
options: lifting, restraining, equanimity; when clarity and calm balance, keep it effortlessly — that is equanimity
quiz.why: "Further lifting a sunken mind, restraining an agitated one, and cultivating excellent equanimity from time to time." Venerable Miào Jìng: when clarity and calm are balanced, you let it effortlessly maintain them — that is equanimity.

quiz.q: Free of overestimation, what does one know one has freed the mind from, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi describe it?
options: only from active affliction, not latent seeds; outside absorption, objects still stir affliction — too strong ones even within
quiz.why: "Through this, one remains free of overestimation, truly knowing for oneself: 'I have only gained freedom of mind from affliction's active manifestation.'" Master Cháng Bǎi: out of absorption, affliction still arises whenever an object appears; if the object is too great or too lovely, even in absorption one may fail to hold firm.

quiz.q: For the fourth conditioning, pliancy, what minimum condition does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: at least access concentration; once the mind is pliant, the body follows
quiz.why: "Fourth, pliancy: with pure faith leading the way, gladness arises in the mind; through that gladness, the grossness of evil states is gradually calmed." Master Cháng Bǎi: the bliss of pliancy requires at least access concentration; after the mind becomes pliant, the body follows.

quiz.q: What is the seventh conditioning, volition, and what image does Venerable Miào Jìng use?
options: the mind's activity — like a commander directing an army
quiz.why: "Seventh, volition: the mind's own activity." Venerable Miào Jìng: like many troops needing a commander to direct them.
